text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 6 in history.
1421 - Henry VI, the last Lancastrian king of England, born. He was only eight months old at the time of his succession.
1492 - Christopher Columbus discovered the island of Hispaniola, now divided between Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
1732 - Warren Hastings, British administrator and first governor-general of Bengal, born.
1857 - Sir Colin Campbell's British troops defeated Sepoy mutineers at the battle of Cawnpore in India.
1877 - Thomas Edison demonstrated the first sound recording, reciting "Mary had a Little Lamb" at West Orange, New Jersey.
1882 - Anthony Trollope, English novelist, born. Best known for his series of novels set in the imaginary English county of Barsetshire.
1889 - Jefferson Davis, American statesman and president of the Confederate States of America during the U.S. Civil War, died.
1906 - Britain granted self-government to the Transvaal and Orange River colonies in South Africa.
1907 - One of the worst coal mine disasters in U.S. history occurred, killing 361 at Mononagh, West Virginia.
1914 - The Polish town of Lodz fell to German troops.
1916 - The German army entered Bucharest.
1917 - The Finnish parliament declared its independence after being an autonomous Grand Duchy of Russia since 1809.
1921 - The Irish Free State was set up as an independent member of the British Commonwealth.
1964 - President Antonio Segni of Italy resigned due to ill health.
1971 - India recognised the Democratic Republic of Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan; Pakistan responded by breaking off diplomatic relations.
1975 - The Balcombe Street Siege began in London when four IRA gunmen took a middle-aged couple hostage. The siege lasted six days.
1978 - A referendum in Spain approved a new constitution, providing for a constitutional monarchy and a parliamentary form of government.
1982 - Seventeen people died in a bomb explosion at a public house in Ballykelly, County Londonderry.
1988 - Roy Orbison, one of the greatest stars in American rock and country music, died; he wrote and sang such hits as "Only the Lonely", "Pretty Woman" and "Running Scared".
1989 - The worst mass killing in Canadian history took place when a gunman shot dead 14 women students at the University of Montreal before killing himself.
1989 - A huge truck bomb devastated the headquarters of Colombia's security and intelligence agency, killing 67 people.
1990 - President Saddam Hussein ordered all foreign hostages held in Iraq and Kuwait to be freed in a major concession to head off the threat of war.
1992 - Swiss voters rejected their government's plan to join a new 19-nation European free trade zone in a referendum that exposed deep rifts between the country's major language groups.
1995 - A Russian Aeroflot Tu-154 with 97 people on board went missing; the wreckage was eventually found on November 18 about 30 miles inland from the Tatar Strait.
